hints.title: Reverse In-Order Traversal
hints.text: In a sorted hierarchy, all values strictly greater than node reside in its right subtree or in ancestors whose left subtrees contain node. Visit nodes in descending order: right, node, left.

hints.title: Running Suffix Sum
hints.text: Maintain an accumulator variable of all visited values. When arriving at a node from its right subtree, add node value to the accumulator and overwrite node value with that total.

hints.title: Left Subtree Recursion
hints.text: After updating the current node value with the running sum, proceed to traverse the left subtree so its elements can inherit the accumulated sum.

hints.title: See the blueprint
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def bstToGst(self, root: Optional[TreeNode]) -> Optional[TreeNode]:
        self.total = 0
        def traverse(node: Optional[TreeNode]):
            if not node:
                return
            traverse(node.right)
            self.total += node.val
            node.val = self.total
            traverse(node.left)
        traverse(root)
        return root
```

variables: N: number of nodes in tree
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Recomputing the sum of greater keys for each node independently takes O(N^2) time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: A single reverse in-order traversal updates all node keys in-place in O(N) time and O(H) call stack.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should recognize that reverse in-order (right -> node -> left) visits keys in descending order.
complexity.notes: Mutates tree in-place; H is O(log N) average and O(N) worst case.
